cases.translation: And now the enchantress winter herself is coming
cases.explain: Зима is the grammatical subject of идет (is coming), so it stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: С окрестных ___ уже снега сбежали мутными ручьями.
cases.translation: From the surrounding hills the snows have already run off in muddy streams
cases.explain: The preposition с (from) governs the genitive plural, so горы becomes гор.

cases.sentence: Пчела за данью полевой Летит из ___ восковой.
cases.translation: The bee flies for its tribute of the field out of its waxen cell
cases.explain: The preposition из (out of) governs the genitive case, so келья becomes кельи.

cases.translation: The inscription speaks to the newcomer
cases.explain: The verb говорит (speaks/tells) takes a dative indirect object, so пришелец becomes пришельцу.

cases.sentence: Улан был должен ехать с нею в ___.
cases.translation: The uhlan had to travel with her to his regiment
cases.explain: The preposition в expressing motion toward a destination governs the accusative, so полк stays полк.

cases.translation: When everyone came out onto the porch
cases.explain: The preposition на with the verb of motion вышли (came out) governs the accusative, so крыльцо stays крыльцо.

cases.sentence: Над этой ___ усмиренной Качал таинственный венок.
cases.translation: Above this humbled funerary urn a mysterious wreath used to sway
cases.explain: The preposition над (above) governs the instrumental case, so урна becomes урной.

cases.translation: Here Petrovsky Castle is surrounded by its own oak grove
cases.explain: The passive participle окружен (surrounded) requires the instrumental of the surrounding agent, so дубрава becomes дубравой.

cases.sentence: Она глядит. Забытый в ___ кий на бильярде отдыхал.
cases.translation: She looks. A forgotten cue rested on the billiard table in the hall
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating static location requires the prepositional case, so зал becomes зале.

reading.ru: Гонимы вешними лучами, С окрестных гор уже снега, Сбежали мутными ручьями На потопленные луга.
reading.question: What natural process opens this chapter, describing the arrival of spring?
options: Snow driven by spring rays runs off the hills in muddy streams onto flooded meadows
A blizzard buries the fields in fresh snow
A drought dries up all the rivers
Autumn leaves fall onto frozen ground
reading.correct: Snow driven by spring rays runs off the hills in muddy streams onto flooded meadows
reading.explain: The chapter opens describing snow, chased by spring's rays, running off the hills onto the flooded meadows.

reading.ru: Как грустно мне твое явление, Весна, весна, пора любви!
reading.question: How does the narrator react to the arrival of spring, contrary to expectation?
options: He finds its arrival sad, despite it being the season of love
He is filled with pure joy
He says spring never truly arrives in Russia
reading.correct: He finds its arrival sad, despite it being the season of love
reading.explain: The narrator laments, 'how sad your appearance is to me, spring, spring, season of love!'

reading.ru: Пойдемте слушать шум дубравный Над безыменной рекой, В деревне, где Евгений мой.
reading.question: Where does the narrator invite the reader to go and listen to the sound of the oak grove?
options: To the village, by an unnamed river, where Onegin lived
reading.correct: To the village, by an unnamed river, where Onegin lived
reading.explain: The narrator invites the reader to the village by an unnamed river, 'where my Evgeny' had lived.

reading.ru: Там виден камень гробовой В тени двух сосен устарелых.
reading.question: What is visible in the shade of two old pine trees?
reading.correct: A gravestone
reading.explain: The text says 'there a gravestone is visible in the shade of two aged pines' — Lensky's grave.

reading.ru: Владимир Ленский здесь лежит, Погибший рано, смертью смелых.
reading.question: Whose grave inscription is this, and how is his death described?
options: Vladimir Lensky's, who perished young, dying the death of the brave
reading.correct: Vladimir Lensky's, who perished young, dying the death of the brave
reading.explain: The gravestone reads 'Vladimir Lensky lies here, who perished young, the death of the brave.'

reading.ru: Но ныне памятник унылый забыт.
reading.question: What has happened to Lensky's grave monument by the time of the narration?
options: It has become a popular pilgrimage site
It has been destroyed by vandals
It has been replaced with a grand statue
reading.correct: It has been forgotten
reading.explain: The text says 'but now the dreary monument is forgotten,' with the path to it overgrown.

reading.ru: Мой бедный Ленский, изнывая, недолго плакала она.
reading.question: How long did Olga mourn for Lensky, according to the narrator?
options: For the rest of her life
She refused to mourn at all
reading.correct: Not for very long
reading.explain: The narrator notes wistfully that his poor Lensky was pined for, but 'she did not weep for long.'

reading.ru: Улан умел ее пленить.
reading.question: Who captivates Olga's affections after Lensky's death?
reading.correct: An uhlan (cavalry officer)
reading.explain: The text says 'the uhlan knew how to captivate her,' referring to a cavalry officer who wins Olga's heart.

reading.ru: И вот уж с ним пред алтарем она стыдливо под венцом стоит.
reading.question: What ceremony does Olga soon undergo with the uhlan?
options: Her wedding, standing bashfully before the altar under the wedding crown
reading.correct: Her wedding, standing bashfully before the altar under the wedding crown
reading.explain: The text describes Olga standing shyly before the altar, under the wedding crown, marrying the uhlan.

reading.ru: Улан, своей невольник доли, был должен ехать с нею в полк.
reading.question: Why must Olga's new husband take her away after the wedding?
options: As a prisoner of his duty, he must travel with her to his regiment
He is being exiled for a crime
He wants to show her off in Moscow
He is retiring from the army
reading.correct: As a prisoner of his duty, he must travel with her to his regiment
reading.explain: The text says the uhlan, 'a captive of his own fate,' had to travel with her to his regiment.

reading.ru: Но Таня плакать не могла.
reading.question: How does Tatiana react while everyone else weeps at Olga's departure?
reading.correct: She could not cry
reading.explain: While others wept, the text says 'but Tanya could not cry,' only turning deathly pale.

reading.ru: Как тень она без цели бродит.
reading.question: How does Tatiana wander after Olga leaves, feeling utterly alone?
options: She refuses to leave her room
reading.correct: Like a shadow, aimlessly
reading.explain: The text says 'like a shadow she wanders without purpose,' finding no comfort anywhere.

reading.ru: Шла, шла, и вдруг перед собою с холма господский видит дом.
reading.question: What does Tatiana suddenly see as she walks and walks during one of her solitary wanderings?
options: The manor house from atop a hill
reading.correct: The manor house from atop a hill
reading.explain: The text says she walked and walked, and suddenly from a hill she sees the master's house — Onegin's home.

reading.ru: К ней лая кинулись собаки.
reading.question: What greets Tatiana as she enters the deserted courtyard of Onegin's house?
reading.correct: Dogs rush at her, barking
reading.explain: The text says 'dogs rushed at her, barking,' as she entered the empty courtyard.

reading.ru: И Таня входит в дом пустой, где жил недавно наш герой.
reading.question: Whose empty house does Tatiana finally enter?
options: Onegin's, where our hero had recently lived
reading.correct: Onegin's, where our hero had recently lived
reading.explain: The text says 'Tanya enters the empty house where our hero had recently lived' — Onegin's manor.

reading.ru: Она глядит. Забытый в зале кий на бильярде отдыхал.
reading.question: What forgotten object does Tatiana notice resting on the billiard table?
reading.correct: A billiard cue
reading.explain: The text describes 'a forgotten cue resting on the billiard table' in the hall.

reading.ru: И лорда Байрона портрет.
reading.question: Whose portrait does Tatiana see in Onegin's study?
reading.correct: Lord Byron's
reading.explain: Among the objects in the study, the text mentions 'a portrait of Lord Byron.'

reading.ru: Хотя мы знаем, что Евгений издавна чтение разлюбил, однако ж несколько творений он из опалы исключил.
reading.question: Despite having fallen out of love with reading, what did Onegin still keep?
options: A few select works he exempted from his general disfavor
Every book he had ever owned
Nothing at all; he burned his library
reading.correct: A few select works he exempted from his general disfavor
reading.explain: The text says that although Onegin had long fallen out of love with reading, he still excepted a few works from his disfavor.

reading.ru: Татьяна видит с трепетанием, какую мыслью, замечанием бывал Онегин поражен.
reading.question: What does Tatiana examine with trembling interest in Onegin's books?
options: The thoughts and remarks that used to strike Onegin, marked in the margins
reading.correct: The thoughts and remarks that used to strike Onegin, marked in the margins
reading.explain: The text says Tatiana, trembling, sees which thoughts and remarks used to strike Onegin, evident from his marginal notes.

reading.ru: Буянов сватался, отказ.
reading.question: What happened when Buyanov proposed to Tatiana, according to her mother's account?
options: Her mother arranged the marriage anyway
reading.correct: He was refused
reading.explain: The mother recounts that 'Buyanov proposed, [and was met with] a refusal.'

reading.ru: И наша дева насладилась дорожной скукою вполне.
reading.question: How does Tatiana experience the long journey to Moscow?
options: She fully experiences the tedium/boredom of the road
She finds it thrilling and adventurous
She sleeps through the entire trip
She enjoys every stop along the way
reading.correct: She fully experiences the tedium/boredom of the road
reading.explain: The text says wryly that 'our maiden fully enjoyed the boredom of the road,' traveling slowly to Moscow.

reading.ru: Москва, как много в этом звуке для сердца русского слилось.
reading.question: What famous sentiment does the narrator express about the word 'Moscow'?
options: How much is contained in that sound for the Russian heart
That Moscow means nothing to true Russians
That Moscow is inferior to Petersburg
That the word has no special meaning at all
reading.correct: How much is contained in that sound for the Russian heart
reading.explain: The narrator exclaims 'Moscow, how much has merged in that sound for the Russian heart,' expressing deep patriotic feeling.

reading.ru: Ей-богу, сцена из романа.
reading.question: How does the old aunt describe the family reunion when Tatiana arrives in Moscow?
options: As a scene straight out of a novel
As something to be kept secret
reading.correct: As a scene straight out of a novel
reading.explain: The elderly relative exclaims about the reunion, 'By God, it's a scene from a novel.'

reading.ru: Татьяна вслушаться желает в беседы, в общий разговор, но всех в гостиной занимает такой бессвязный пошлый вздор.
reading.question: What frustrates Tatiana about the conversations at Moscow social gatherings?
options: The talk is disjointed, vulgar nonsense that occupies everyone
No one will speak to her at all
The conversations are all about her directly
reading.correct: The talk is disjointed, vulgar nonsense that occupies everyone
reading.explain: The text says Tatiana wishes to listen closely, but the drawing room is absorbed only in 'disconnected, vulgar nonsense.'

reading.ru: Но та, которую не смею Тревожить лиру моей, Как величавая луна, Средь жен и дев блестит одна.
reading.question: How does the narrator describe the mysterious woman he hesitates to name at the Moscow ball?
options: Like a majestic moon, shining alone among the wives and maidens
As already known to be Tatiana's rival
As a foreign princess visiting Moscow
reading.correct: Like a majestic moon, shining alone among the wives and maidens
reading.explain: The narrator, coy about naming her, compares this woman to 'a majestic moon' shining alone among the women present.

highlight.question: What information does the inscription on the monument provide?
highlight.explain: The inscription tells of Vladimir Lensky lying buried, who died young and bravely at a specific age.

highlight.question: What is Tatyana's emotional condition after her separation?
sentences: Как тень она без цели бродит,
Нигде, ни в чём ей нет отрад,
highlight.explain: Separated from Onegin by fate, Tatyana wanders without purpose, finding no solace anywhere.

highlight.question: How does Tatyana regard her surroundings now?
highlight.explain: Everything around her seems precious and cherished, bringing bittersweet comfort to her troubled soul.

highlight.question: What conflicting descriptions does Tatyana apply to Onegin?
highlight.explain: She views him as both a creature of heaven and a prideful demon, struggling to understand his nature.

highlight.question: What change occurs in nature as the summer ends?
highlight.explain: Golden autumn arrives and nature becomes trembling and pale, like an adorned sacrificial victim.

highlight.question: Why is winter travel described favorably?
sentences: Как стих без мысли в песне модной —
highlight.explain: Winter roads are smooth and pleasant for travel, just as a road without thought complements a fashionable song.
